lines.en: : Oh. That was quick.
: Told you it was a convenient power! Just one more perk of being a time-janitor.
: You really need to come up with a different name for-
: Why are you still wearing that?
: It’s surprisingly comfy. I don’t blame your friend one bit for looking so tired all the time.
: So, like...how much of my life do you watch exactly? Because, whatever the amount may be, I’d appreciate it if you could drop it down to zero from this point on.
: No can do, buckaroo. I need to stay in the loop, pun not intended, to make sure things don’t get too messed up since they could directly impact my continued existence.
: Sorry, are things not already “too messed up?” Because they seem pretty fucking messed up, Himawari.

: Yeah, well, you live in a world that’s essentially just a side-effect of your imaginary friend’s imaginary desires. Of course something like that wouldn’t be stable when it technically shouldn’t exist at all.
: Calling her an “imaginary friend” is a little reductive, don’t you think? She still thinks. She still feels. And I’m almost positive she has no idea about what she is if what you say is true.
: Why would she? Assuming you’re the only fake person in a sea of real ones is something so depressing and weird that I don’t even think you could do it. And you do all sorts of weird stuff.
: Maybe here I do. It’s hard not to when you’re surrounded by...equally weird shit. I was normal in Aomori, though. At least...comparatively.
: I think you’re a little weirdo who’s never been normal anywhere. But yeah, I think I get what you’re saying.
: Do you, like...remember any of it? Or is everything that happened just...
: Hm? Of course I remember it. I brought up the purikura booths, didn’t I?
: But...how? You erased that Himawari, didn’t you? I assumed everything just...went with her.
: Nope! All up here. Every last minute of it. That’s how I set it up.
: Set it up?...
: Think of the Himawari in Aomori as a solar panel and me as the battery. She collects memories and I absorb them. It’d be hard to do my job if that wasn’t the case.
: There will be more soon too.
: More...Himawaris?
: Yup! I’m still trying to work out the kinks, but I have big plans for the future. I want solar panels everywhere. Don’t tell anybody I told you that, though. It’s a secret.
: But...I thought you said we only get one wish and Aomori was yours? Do you...get another now that it’s been destroyed?
: It’s not destroyed at all. It’ll start over soon with a new me and a new you who wound up there due to fate or choice or whatever it is that leads people anywhere.
: Just because you had to witness the fall of one due to my colossal mix-up doesn’t mean there aren’t millions of other Aomoris out there born from someone else’s wishes.
: That’s why it took me so long to find you. I didn’t realize you were there at all for the first two months.
: I was, like...seriously freaking out. And it only got worse once I figured out what happened since I knew taking you back would break both of your hearts.
: You’re surprisingly fine, though. Do you actually not love me at all?
: Of course I do. I’m just still trying to understand the...logistics of this place.
: We call it the Wishing Well. For reasons I’m sure you can figure out on your own. And yeah, it’s hard to ever really understand it without zooming out to see the big picture.
: I know when I was first starting out, it helped me to think about it like the stars. Just a big ole’ scatter plot but without any logic or reason to it, with each star being a different world.
: We have names and classifications for all of them, just as we do the gods themselves. But with more popping up or fizzling out every day, it’s definitely overwhelming at times.
: We are extremely understaffed too. You’d think the organization literally pulling the levers that guide humanity would have its shit together, but nope. Just as chaotic as any other megacorp.
: How did you even get involved in any of this? I don’t understand. You seemed so...normal and...almost directionless just yesterday.
: I am sorry, but that information is classified. I am unable to disclose the specifics of our recruitment program.
: Just know that only the best of the best are selected. To which I am a clear choice, as I’m sure you’d agree.
: Yeah...just a little surprised to see you’re still hiding information from me. I assumed “origins of the world” would be a little higher on the classified priority list than your hiring process.
: You have clearly never worked for a megacorp.
: That said! I will answer any question I find directly relevant to your mission of escaping from this place to reunite with me under happier circumstances.
: Then, could you at least tell me what your “home world” is like? The one where the original you is from? Because the fact that you needed to wish for a better world at all is-
: Indicative that things weren’t perfect there, right?
: Like, maybe there was a real apocalypse that killed you and mom and pulled me into all of this? Or maybe I just wasn’t as cute there and needed to create a world in which I was?
: Are you just going to answer my question with other rhetorical questions or do you have an actual response?
: I’ll need more time for that one, if that’s okay. I need to be careful about what I say to you since I don’t want to negatively influence your actions from this point on.
: So you won’t answer anything directly relevant. Just positively relevant.
: We have less than twenty four hours together and you’re going to waste it on pedantry?
: That’s all?...
: Yeah...
: You didn’t think this would last forever, did you?
: No, but...I wanted more than a day at least. Ayane isn’t even able to-
: We’ll have plenty of time someday, but...
: Today is not that day. I still have a job to do. And so do you.
: If we’re not able to put our feelings aside, we’ll never get you out of here. And that’s something that absolutely needs to happen if we’re ever going to meet again.
: Hah...
: On the bright side, we got to spend four whole months together. And they were the best four months I’ve had in a very long time.
: They were the best four months I’ve ever had. I don’t know how I’m supposed to just...go back to normal after this.
: You can always change what “normal” is. And you probably should too since you’ve been pretty unhelpful concerning your own rescue mission.
: Yeah, well we’ll see how effective I am now that I’m also aware the girl I’ve been hung up on forever can’t exist in the same world as me.
: It’s tougher than it sounds. And it sounds pretty tough to begin with, doesn’t it?
: Yeah...tough is an understatement.
: What’s the plan now, then? You mentioned something about, uhh...reformatting people?
: Think of what you saw back in Aomori, just on a smaller and sometimes, uhh...different scale.
: Different how? Because I kept it together, but what I saw back up north was haunting and I’d prefer to not see it again if I don’t have to.
: I warned you it wouldn’t be pretty, didn’t I?
: Yeah, but that could mean anything.
: It’s precisely because it could mean anything that it won’t be pretty.
: The end of the world doesn’t just come and go for everyone. People fight back sometimes. Like cornered animals finally understanding the gravity of the threat they face.
: Fight back...how? Against the world itself?
: Depends on what they see. Or what they think they see. But most of the time, they just turn into dolls.
: Dolls?
: Limp and lifeless. Glassy eyes and skin that’s cold to the touch. Just they aren’t actually lifeless in most cases. They’re sort of just...dormant. Waiting for the world to start turning again.
: And...the one’s who aren’t like that? What becomes of them?
: Shi-chan normally. Or any other specialist.
: Your friend?
: Careful. I don’t want her to hear me call her that and she might be waiting around here somewhere.
: The specialists are the ones who take care of the bodies who need restoring, though. They typically require a little extra work to prevent them from going haywire again.
: Himawari, if these are girls I care about, I don’t want to see them-
: Keep your eyes on me if it makes you more comfortable. I don’t want you to have to see stuff like that either.
: I’m used to it now, but I’d be lying if I didn’t say it ruined many a day for me back in the beginning.
: It can still be scary, I admit. But I’m a little less scared knowing you’re with me. So please don’t chicken out.
: I’m in it for the long haul at this point. Just don’t hold it against me if the sight of blood triggers the same trauma that likely snowballed into this universe spawning in the first place-
: AAAAAHHHH!
: What is it? You don’t see someone from school, do-
: RABBIT!
: Sorry. Did I say “rabbit?” I meant Sana.
: Don’t worry. I understood the callback.
: She really is just...limp, huh?
: She was probably hanging out over here when time stopped and just plopped over. That’s how it goes most of the time, to be honest. Just one more reason we call them dolls.
: What now then?
: Now, you get a behind-the-scenes peek at how all of the girls you know have their memories and perceptions altered any time the world reboots.
: Think of it like a virus scan, but for humans instead of computers. We purge them of information that might make the world less stable and make sure that all the interpersonal stuff stays.
: We refresh their inhibitors too, which is what keeps most of them from ever catching onto the fact that they’re living in a fabricated reality at all.
: And the reason I say “most of them” is because girls in this world are actually catching on for some reason.
: Does that not happen in other worlds? Does everyone just stay oblivious?
: Most of the time, yeah. People are so afraid of death that like 95%% of the worlds generated via wishes involve an infinite timeline. So dealing with this is super common, all things considered.
: We’ve had people become somewhat “aware” in the past when it comes to other worlds. Never on this scale, though, with multiple people gaining awareness at the same time.
: Most timelines are much longer too. And while there are definitely a good number of “forever young” aspirants out there, their worlds aren’t typically restricted to just a single school year.
: In the grand scheme of things, basically everything about this world makes it look like a repeatedly malfunctioning version of a typical wish. Which is likely because-
: Because it comes from Maya and not someone “real.”
: Good job, Dad! You’re so smart! I’m so proud of you!
: Thank you. I will ignore the very obvious sarcasm and take these words to heart. I have uncovered the secrets of the world and am now ready to leave.
: It’s this stuff that ultimately caught the attention of the higher-ups in the first place and led to them realizing what this place is.
: A world that, in itself, is a bit of a virus. Or perhaps even a bootleg since it’s clearly based on the world you brought Maya into.
: Wait...
: Then, could she continue to exist if we get back to that world? The one where she exists but this place doesn’t?
: I’m not sure. Theoretically, yes. There are plenty of worlds out there where wishes walk among us.

: But I think the fact that Maya was capable of doing this in the first place is going to make it a lot harder for the gods to justify keeping her around, knowing they could be undermined at any minute.
: Which isn’t even touching upon the fact that it’d be extremely unlikely for you to end up with Mom in a world where Maya continues to exist.
: Me being here at all leads me to believe she can’t exist in any form in order for the future to properly unfold.
: But there’s technically a chance you’re wrong, right?
: There’s technically a chance you could be elected as prime minister too. But that doesn’t mean it’s going to happen or that you should get your hopes up for it.
: Himawari-
: Dad — I know you love her and I know you want to save her. You would have never wished for her at all if that wasn’t the case.
: But I am concerned about you and Mom and that’s it.
: Saving Maya is beyond my capabilities and, frankly, beyond my desires as well. If I let myself get attached to others the way you do, I’d have never been chosen for this job in the first place.
: What about Sana then? You clearly care about her if there’s still a place for her in your dream world.

: Just because I wished for something doesn’t mean I have complete control over it. I just wanted a perfect little life with my parents where all three of us had everything we wanted. And Mom wanted Sana.
: I do like her. Mostly as an adult, though. She’s kind of...a lot at this age. And not in a good way.
: I actually posed as her on this very beach a few years ago and had an entire conversation with you. That’s obviously not something you’d remember, though.
: I’m not exactly allowed to be a recurring figure in your life. Something about a “conflict of interest” or whatever. Little do they know, that’s exactly why I signed on. I’m so evil, aren’t I?
: You’ve appeared to me before?...
: Mhm. A bunch of times. Sometimes it’s just as a spectator, though.
: I don’t always need to be involved. It’s enough just to be near you.
: I think my Sana impression might need some work, though. You saw through me pretty easily and I just looked weird and forceful. Probably because I had to flirt with my dad.
: Did I know it was you?...Like, you?
: Nope.
: But maybe next time you will?
: Now, please excuse me while I reformat this gremlin.
Himawari places her hand on the back of Sana’s head and I need to force away what I can only call “suppressed PTSD” as I flash back to what happened in Aomori just a short while ago.

And while I can’t imagine the image of her being broken down into pixels will soon (if ever) depart from my memory, I can make it less painful by superimposing her true self over it as that is one vision I won’t ever suppress.
: So do you, like...feel anything when you do that?
: What — like physically? Or emotionally?
: Uhh...both?
: Physically, it’s like a cross between a dull vibration and a static-shock effect. So pretty much how you’d expect it to feel based on looking at the result.
: Emotionally, it’s a little weirder. Like a person’s emotions, thoughts, and memories are flowing into you so you can properly quarantine them.
: Sometimes it hurts, sometimes it doesn’t.
: Does it hurt right now?
: To be honest, I’m not sure it will ever hurt again after Aomori.
: You went back there again?
: Ah! Shi-chan! There you are!
